contract: Durable mail and room continuation chains over a consumer-owned Ecto Repo on PostgreSQL 16 in three Piece-owned tables (chains, links, messages) that Migration.install/1 creates and protects with the state/tenant-isolation floor. new/2 binds a declaration of 1..64 message names, each built with core/payload-schema, and its identity {id, version, SHA-256 of the canonical JSON}; verify/1 runs the floor check per table. open/3 creates a chain and its first link (equal bytes and declaration duplicate, else conflict; a held run_id or unit_identity is identity_in_use). put/3 refuses, in order and before any write, a bad shape, an undeclared name, another schema version, a payload that fails the schema, a caller transaction, another isolation level, an unknown chain, another declaration, a stored message_id with other bytes (equal bytes duplicate, wherever addressed) and a chain at max_pending open messages; mail to any link's run_id goes to the chain. Every write after open/3 takes the chain row FOR UPDATE first: claim/3 gives the delivering message again, else stopped, else the oldest pending message to the live tip; settle/3 records applied, not_applied (pending again) or one of four refusals (record_size also stops the link), repeats are duplicate or not_delivering; plan_rollover/3 records the successor's pin on the tip; rollover/3 closes the tip and inserts exactly one successor that keeps the pin unless an explicit change, refusing unknown_link, already_rolled_over (equal bytes repeat the answer), delivery_unsettled, plan_mismatch and identity_in_use. chain/3 pages links (1..256) with the tip and its carry; status/3 reads a message's state. Canonical JSON (compact Jason, keys sorted by bytes) decides every comparison and the 65,536-byte bounds; fixed error atoms, log: false, no telemetry, no Run start, engine call or timer.
limits: The state/tenant-isolation limits apply: the table owner can turn forcing off or drop the policies, and a superuser or BYPASSRLS role ignores them.
READ COMMITTED is a consumer Need that the Piece checks but cannot set.
The sender, the terminal outcome, the change reference and the not_applied and refused readings are host-vouched.
A message is delivered to exactly one link, not exactly once end to end; the engine's input IDs decide what a Run saw.

Mail payloads hold people's text and have no delete, expiry or erasure; dead tuples, WAL and backups keep content until PostgreSQL reclaims them. Links are never pruned, so a chain grows by one row per rollover.
An :unavailable result can be an unknown outcome when the connection is lost during COMMIT; a retry with the same request is safe.

log: false silences only the Logger: the consumer Repo's query telemetry still receives the parameters, including payloads and carries, and a Repo that logs queries logs each transaction's begin and commit.

Two concurrent rollovers of different chains of one tenant naming the same successor run_id or unit_identity can both pass the identity check; the later one fails on the unique index as unavailable and its retry is identity_in_use.
No Run start, engine call, timer, notifier, priority, expiry or dead-lettering.
Finite listed scenarios on one local PostgreSQL 16, including barrier-controlled races; not proofs of isolation, ordering or atomicity.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios on the worker's own disposable PostgreSQL 16 database behind a fail-closed target guard, with DBConnection.ConnectionPool Repos (not the Sandbox) whose every application connection SET ROLEs to the ELZ-285 application role (ELZOO_TEST_APP_ROLE; fail, not skip, when unset) with only the README grants, in random schemas dropped afterwards: 1 each refusal of put/3 steps 1-4 and 6-9 leaves the three tables, read inside transact/3 under the tenant's scope, unchanged, two failing steps give the earlier step's refusal (1-4 inside a caller transaction, 5 before 6, 6 before 7, 7 before 8, 8 before 9), and new/2 refuses a schema that does not build, 0 and 65 names, bad names and bounds; the declaration identity equals SHA-256 of a hand-written canonical text, and stored payload and carry texts equal hand-written canonical JSON (sorted keys, escapes, floats, big integers), and a 1,025-digit integer in a payload and a carry is claimed, settled and read back exactly; 2 message_id 155 and 156 bytes, payload and carry of 65,536 and 65,537 canonical bytes, depth 32 and 33, max_pending 0, 1, 65,536 and 65,537, text, unit identity, outcome and ref bounds; 3 duplicate and conflict for open/3 (each field, another declaration, after a rollover) and put/3 (each field, the chain and closed and live link run_ids), and two open/3 calls held behind a SHARE lock until both inserts wait in pg_locks give one chain and one duplicate, or one conflict; 4 FIFO over three messages and a not_applied settle; 5 mailbox_full at max_pending 1 and 2 with duplicates at the bound; 6 mail to a closed link's run_id is claimed for the tip; 7 a claim and a rollover queued behind another connection's chain row lock, each seen waiting in pg_locks: claim first gives delivery_unsettled, rollover first gives a claim for the successor; 8 two rollovers of one link behind the same barrier commit one successor, equal bytes give the same seq and other bytes already_rolled_over, and direct inserts of a second successor fail on the predecessor index and the primary key; 9 a connection dropped after claim/3 gives the same message to the same link; 10 settle with each result and reason, duplicate and not_delivering repeats, another link, refused messages do not block a rollover, record_size stops the link and claim/3 returns stopped; 11 the pin kept, changed with change_ref, plans replaced with previous, plan_mismatch, not_tip and unknown_link; 12 identity_in_use for successors and opens within a tenant, accepted in another; 13 chain/3 paging at limit 1 and 256 over 258 links with more and the tip carry, status/3 of each state and unknown_message; 14 verify/1 passes and names a table without forced row security, T1 gets unknown_chain for T2's chain, direct T2 inserts and DELETEs fail 42501, every function succeeds with only the README grants; 15 a caller transaction gives in_transaction for every function with no query on the Repo's telemetry and verify/1 the same inside and outside, a repeatable-read Repo gives isolation for every write with nothing written, a missing schema gives unavailable, a bad prefix raises the fixed ArgumentError, and a Repo started with log: :error logs only begin and commit, no Piece statement. Skipping the payload check fails case 1; dropping the chain row lock of rollover/3 with the barrier on the link row lets both rollovers wait on the link UPDATE and the second fail on the key (unavailable), failing case 8; removing the delivery_unsettled check leaves a message delivering to a closed link, failing case 7; dropping log: false from the Piece's queries fails the log case (negative controls). Finite scenarios, not proofs.

PostgreSQL 16 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row locks queue waiters in order, read-committed statement snapshots read the committed row after a lock wait, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waits for a concurrent insert of the same key, unique and primary key indexes refuse a duplicate row, and row-level security and table privileges fail with 42501; upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex 0.22.4.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transact/2 commit and rollback on an error tuple, in_transaction?/0, Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query/4 with log: false and migration execute/1 are upstream behavior.
Jason 1.4.5 encode!/1 with default options and Jason.OrderedObject give the compact encoding in the given key order with the README escapes and shortest float form.

OTP 29.1.2 crypto:hash(sha256, Data) computes the declaration identity over the canonical encoding, and json:decode/3 with null as nil reads stored payloads and carries back, keeping integers of any length.
Elixir String.valid?/1, the utf8 binary pattern and Regex anchors for the text and name rules, and binary term order for the canonical key sort.

The consumer runs the migration as the table owner in an existing schema, connects the application as a non-owner, non-bypass role with only the README grants and READ COMMITTED transactions, calls verify/1 at startup, keeps one declaration per chain, and vouches for senders, outcomes, change references and settle readings.

telemetry.contract: The Piece emits no events and no logs; its queries pass log: false, and the consumer Repo's query telemetry is unchanged (a limit: it receives the parameters).

config.contract: The binding from new/2 (exactly repo: and prefix:, and a declaration of id, version, max_pending 1..65,536 and 1..64 message names with schema versions and schemas, else invalid_declaration) is the only configuration, fixed for the value's life. Contract bounds are fixed: 128-byte tenant, chain, Run, pin and sender IDs, 155-byte message_id, 160-byte unit identity, 256-byte change ref, 64-byte outcome, 65,536 canonical bytes and depth 32 for payload and carry, chain/3 limit 1..256, 63-byte prefix.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; the consumer owns the Repo, the migration and the database roles.
